Score: dot product of Q and K, scaled by √d_k
Weights: softmax of scores gives attention weights
Output: weighted sum of V vectors
Captures dependencies regardless of distance
Parallelizable: no sequential dependency like RNN

question: What is multi-head attention and why is it used?
hinglish_explanation: Single attention ek type ki relationship capture karta hai. Multi-head: parallel mein multiple attention heads run karo, har head different relationship capture kare. Head 1: syntactic (subject-verb), Head 2: semantic (pronoun-referent), Head 3: positional. Outputs concatenate karke project karo.
real_life_example: 'She gave him the book that was on the table' - Head 1: 'She'→'gave' (subject-verb), Head 2: 'that'→'book' (reference), Head 3: 'on'→'table' (spatial). Multiple heads = multiple relationship types simultaneously. BERT-base has 12 heads.
how_to_answer: Multiple attention heads running in parallel
Each head: different Q, K, V projection matrices
Each head can attend to different positions/relationships
Concatenate all head outputs, then linear projection
BERT-base: 12 heads, BERT-large: 16 heads, GPT-3: 96 heads
Head dimension = model_dim / num_heads (768/12=64 for BERT)
Ablation shows: different heads learn different linguistic patterns

question: What is positional encoding and why do Transformers need it?
hinglish_explanation: Transformer mein koi recurrence nahi hai - word order ka pata nahi. Positional encoding position information add karta hai. Sinusoidal PE: sin/cos functions different frequencies mein. Learned PE: embeddings train karo position ke liye. RoPE (rotary): modern LLMs mein popular hai. Without PE: 'dog bites man' = 'man bites dog'.
real_life_example: BERT: learned positional embeddings (max 512 tokens). GPT: bhi learned positions. LLaMA/GPT-NeoX: RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding) jo extrapolation bhi allow karta hai - 4K training pe 16K inference possible. ALiBi bhi popular hai.
how_to_answer: Transformers have no inherent notion of token order
Positional encoding injects position information
Sinusoidal: PE(pos,2i) = sin(pos/10000^(2i/d))
Learned: trainable position embedding matrix
RoPE: rotates attention keys/queries by position angle
ALiBi: adds position-based bias to attention scores
Without PE: model treats input as bag of tokens

question: Explain the BERT architecture and its pre-training objectives.
hinglish_explanation: BERT = Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Encoder-only Transformer. Pre-training: (1) MLM - randomly 15% tokens mask karo, predict karo. (2) NSP - do sentences consecutive hain ya nahi predict karo. Fine-tuning: task-specific head add karo. Revolutionized NLP in 2018.
real_life_example: Google Search: BERT integration se search quality dramatically improve hui. 'Can you get medicine for someone pharmacy' - BERT samajhta hai 'for someone' ka context. Fine-tuned BERT: sentiment classification 2% data se SOTA achieve karta hai.
how_to_answer: BERT: encoder-only Transformer, bidirectional context
Architecture: 12 layers, 768 hidden, 12 heads (BERT-base)
Pre-training objective 1: MLM (Masked Language Modeling) - predict masked tokens
Pre-training objective 2: NSP (Next Sentence Prediction) - binary classification
Fine-tuning: add task head, update all parameters on labeled data
Input: [CLS] + tokens + [SEP] (+ tokens2 + [SEP] for pairs)
Dominant NLU model: classification, NER, QA, similarity

question: Explain GPT architecture and how it differs from BERT.
hinglish_explanation: GPT = Generative Pre-trained Transformer. Decoder-only, left-to-right (causal). Pre-training: next token prediction (CLM - Causal Language Modeling). BERT: bidirectional, understanding tasks. GPT: unidirectional, generation tasks. GPT-3/4 scale pe emergent abilities dikhati hain.
real_life_example: ChatGPT: GPT architecture pe based hai. Ek ek token generate karta hai left-to-right. 'The capital of India is ___' → 'New' → 'Delhi'. BERT ye nahi kar sakta directly. GPT-4: 1.7T parameters (rumored), multimodal, reasoning capabilities.
how_to_answer: GPT: decoder-only Transformer, autoregressive left-to-right
Pre-training: Causal Language Modeling (predict next token)
Causal mask: can only attend to previous tokens (no future)
BERT: bidirectional (sees all), GPT: unidirectional (sees left only)
BERT: better for understanding, GPT: better for generation
GPT-3: 175B params, few-shot learning without fine-tuning
Scaling laws: larger GPT models show emergent capabilities

question: What is the T5 model and how does it unify NLP tasks?
hinglish_explanation: T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer) sab NLP tasks ko text-to-text format mein convert karta hai. Classification: 'classify: I love it' → 'positive'. Translation: 'translate English to Hindi: Hello' → 'नमस्ते'. Summarization: 'summarize: long text' → 'short summary'. One model, all tasks!
real_life_example: Single T5 model: 'translate: Good morning' → 'सुप्रभात', 'summarize: <article>' → summary, 'question: what is NLP? context: <passage>' → answer. Prefix decide karta hai task kaunsa hai. Google Search mein T5 use hota hai.
how_to_answer: T5: encoder-decoder Transformer, text-to-text framework
All tasks reformulated as text input → text output
Task prefix specifies what to do: 'translate:', 'summarize:', 'classify:'
Pre-training: span corruption (mask spans, predict them)
Encoder-decoder: good for conditional generation tasks
Sizes: Small(60M) to XXL(11B) parameters
Advantage: single model architecture for all NLP tasks

question: What is the difference between encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder Transformers?
hinglish_explanation: Encoder-only (BERT): bidirectional, understanding tasks (classification, NER). Decoder-only (GPT): left-to-right, generation tasks (text completion, chat). Encoder-decoder (T5, BART): input encode + output generate, conditional generation (translation, summarization). Choose architecture based on task!
real_life_example: Sentiment analysis → BERT (encoder-only). Story writing → GPT (decoder-only). English→Hindi translation → T5/mBART (encoder-decoder). Modern trend: decoder-only (GPT-4, LLaMA) sab tasks kar lete hain with enough scale.
how_to_answer: Encoder-only (BERT, RoBERTa): bidirectional, NLU tasks
Decoder-only (GPT, LLaMA): causal/left-to-right, generation
Encoder-decoder (T5, BART): encode input, decode output
Encoder-only: best for classification, NER, sentence embedding
Decoder-only: best for text generation, chat, completion
Encoder-decoder: best for translation, summarization, QA
Trend: decoder-only models at scale can do all tasks

question: What is Masked Language Modeling (MLM) and how does BERT use it?
hinglish_explanation: MLM: randomly 15% tokens mask karo, model predict kare masked tokens. 'The [MASK] sat on the mat' → predict 'cat'. Bidirectional context use hota hai prediction mein. 15% mein: 80% [MASK], 10% random word, 10% unchanged. Ye trick fine-tuning mein mismatch reduce karti hai.
real_life_example: BERT training: Wikipedia articles leke randomly words mask karo. Model context se guess kare. Like CLOZE test humans ke liye: 'India's capital is ___'. Pre-training ke baad BERT language deeply samajhta hai without any labeled data!
how_to_answer: MLM: randomly mask 15% of input tokens, predict them
Bidirectional: uses both left and right context for prediction
Masking strategy: 80% [MASK], 10% random, 10% unchanged
10% random + 10% unchanged reduces train-test mismatch
Loss: cross-entropy only on masked positions
Different from CLM (GPT): MLM sees all context, CLM sees only left
Foundation of BERT's strong NLU capabilities

question: What is fine-tuning a pre-trained model and what are best practices?
hinglish_explanation: Pre-trained model (BERT/GPT) ko apne specific task pe train karna = fine-tuning. Task-specific head add karo (classifier for classification). Small learning rate (2e-5 to 5e-5). Few epochs (2-4). Less data chahiye vs training from scratch. Transfer learning ka powerful form hai.
real_life_example: Customer complaint classification: BERT pre-trained lelo, classification head add karo, 1000 labeled complaints pe 3 epochs fine-tune karo = 95% accuracy. From scratch same data pe: 65% accuracy. BERT ka general language knowledge transfer hota hai.
how_to_answer: Fine-tuning: adapt pre-trained model to specific downstream task
Add task-specific head (linear layer for classification, etc.)
Small learning rate: 2e-5 to 5e-5 (don't destroy pre-trained weights)
Few epochs: 2-4 typically sufficient
Warmup: linear warmup for first 10% of steps
Weight decay: 0.01 for regularization
Data efficiency: 100-1000 examples often sufficient with fine-tuning

question: What is the difference between BERT, RoBERTa, and ALBERT?
hinglish_explanation: BERT: original, MLM+NSP. RoBERTa: BERT but better training (no NSP, more data, longer training, dynamic masking). ALBERT: smaller BERT (parameter sharing between layers, factorized embedding). RoBERTa > BERT quality. ALBERT same quality in smaller size.
real_life_example: Production deployment: ALBERT-base same accuracy as BERT-base but 18x fewer parameters = mobile-friendly. Research: RoBERTa gives best quality (trained on 160GB text vs BERT's 16GB). Choose based on: accuracy need vs deployment constraints.
how_to_answer: BERT: MLM + NSP pre-training, 110M parameters
RoBERTa: removes NSP, more data (160GB), dynamic masking, longer training
ALBERT: factorized embeddings + cross-layer parameter sharing
RoBERTa > BERT on all benchmarks (better training recipe)
ALBERT: 12x fewer parameters with similar performance
DeBERTa: disentangled attention, currently strongest BERT-variant
Choose: RoBERTa for quality, ALBERT/DistilBERT for efficiency

question: What is causal attention mask and why is it needed in GPT?
hinglish_explanation: GPT generation mein future tokens nahi dekh sakta (cheating hogi!). Causal mask: upper triangular matrix -infinity se fill karo attention scores mein. Softmax ke baad future positions ka weight 0 ho jaata hai. Training mein bhi same mask use hota hai consistency ke liye. BERT mein ye mask nahi hai (bidirectional).
real_life_example: GPT generating 'I love India': 'I' generate karte waqt kuch nahi dekh sakta, 'love' generate karte waqt sirf 'I' dekh sakta, 'India' generate karte waqt 'I love' dekh sakta. Ye causal mask enforce karta hai. Autoregressive nature ensure hoti hai.
how_to_answer: Causal/autoregressive mask prevents attending to future tokens
Implementation: upper triangular matrix of -infinity in attention scores
After softmax: future positions get zero attention weight
Ensures model can only use past tokens for prediction
Required for valid autoregressive generation at inference
Training: apply mask so each position predicts next token
BERT: no mask (bidirectional); GPT: causal mask (left-to-right)

question: What is DistilBERT and how is it created?
hinglish_explanation: DistilBERT = Distilled BERT. Knowledge distillation se BERT-base ka 60% size, 97% performance, 60% faster. Teacher (BERT-large) student (smaller model) ko train karta hai. Student teacher ke soft predictions (probabilities) se seekhta hai - zyada information milti hai hard labels se.
real_life_example: Mobile app pe BERT run karna slow hai (110M params). DistilBERT: 66M params, almost same accuracy, 2x faster. Production APIs mein latency half. HuggingFace ne release kiya - drop-in replacement for BERT with speed benefit.
how_to_answer: DistilBERT: compressed BERT via knowledge distillation
6 layers vs BERT's 12 layers (50% fewer)
97% of BERT's performance, 60% faster, 40% smaller
Distillation: train student on teacher's soft probability outputs
Triple loss: distillation + MLM + cosine embedding loss
No NSP task, no token type embeddings
Ideal for: production deployment, edge devices, real-time apps

question: What is layer normalization and why is it important in Transformers?
hinglish_explanation: Layer norm: ek layer ke outputs ko normalize karo (mean=0, var=1) across features. Batch norm batch ke across normalize karta hai (NLP mein variable lengths ki wajah se problematic). Layer norm stable training deta hai, gradient flow improve karta hai. Pre-norm (before attention) vs post-norm (after attention) debate hai.
real_life_example: Without layer norm: deep transformer training unstable, loss explode hota hai. With layer norm: smooth training, consistent gradients. GPT-2 pre-norm use karta hai (layer norm before attention), original Transformer post-norm. Pre-norm generally more stable.
how_to_answer: Layer normalization: normalize across features for each sample
Unlike batch norm: independent of batch size, works for variable lengths
Applied after each sub-layer in Transformer (attention + FFN)
Stabilizes training of deep networks
Pre-norm: LN before attention (GPT-2 style) - more stable
Post-norm: LN after attention (original Transformer) - better final performance
Learnable scale (γ) and shift (β) parameters

question: What is the feed-forward network in Transformers and what role does it play?
hinglish_explanation: Transformer block: Attention → FFN. FFN = two linear layers with activation: FFN(x) = W2·GELU(W1·x + b1) + b2. Inner dimension 4x model dim (BERT: 768→3072→768). FFN ek position-wise transformation hai - har token independently transform hota hai. Memory/knowledge storage maana jaata hai.
real_life_example: BERT 768-dim → FFN 3072-dim → back to 768-dim. Ye expansion-compression factual knowledge store karta hai. Research shows FFN neurons specific facts encode karte hain - like 'Eiffel Tower is in Paris' ek neuron mein stored hota hai.
how_to_answer: Two linear layers with non-linearity: W2(activation(W1·x + b1)) + b2
Applied identically to each position (position-wise)
Inner dimension typically 4× model dimension
Activation: GELU (BERT), ReLU (original), SwiGLU (LLaMA)
Accounts for ~67% of Transformer parameters
Hypothesized to store factual knowledge
Each FFN layer has independent parameters (not shared)

question: What is the KV-cache and why is it important for efficient inference?
hinglish_explanation: Autoregressive generation mein har new token ke liye pura sequence recompute karna wasteful hai. KV-cache: previous tokens ke Key aur Value vectors cache karo, sirf new token ka Q compute karo. Inference O(n²) se O(n) per step. Memory use badhta hai but computation drastically reduce hota hai.
real_life_example: ChatGPT 1000 token response generate karta hai. Without KV-cache: har token ke liye 1000+ tokens recompute. With KV-cache: sirf naye token ke attention compute, purane cached. 100x speedup! GPU memory mein KV-cache store hota hai - batch size limit karta hai.
how_to_answer: KV-cache: store computed Key and Value tensors from previous steps
During autoregressive generation: only compute new token's Q, K, V
Attend new Q against all cached K,V + new K,V
Reduces per-token computation from O(n) to O(1) attention compute
Memory: grows linearly with sequence length per layer
Major inference optimization: enables real-time LLM serving
Tradeoff: memory usage vs computation speed

question: What is the BART model and how does it combine BERT and GPT?
hinglish_explanation: BART = encoder-decoder model. Encoder BERT-like (bidirectional), Decoder GPT-like (autoregressive). Pre-training: input corrupt karo (mask, delete, shuffle), decoder se reconstruct karo. Denoising autoencoder hai essentially. Summarization ke liye best model tha. T5 jaisa but different pre-training.
real_life_example: News summarization: BART article encode karta hai (encoder), summary generate karta hai (decoder). Facebook ne release kiya. CNN/DailyMail summarization benchmark pe SOTA tha. mBART multilingual version 25 languages support karta hai.
how_to_answer: BART: encoder-decoder combining BERT-style encoder + GPT-style decoder
Pre-training: corrupt input → reconstruct original (denoising)
Corruption: token masking, deletion, permutation, rotation
Encoder: bidirectional (BERT-like), Decoder: autoregressive (GPT-like)
Excellent for: summarization, translation, text generation
Similar to T5 but different pre-training corruption strategy
mBART: multilingual version for cross-lingual generation

question: What is Flash Attention and why is it needed?
hinglish_explanation: Standard attention O(n²) memory use karta hai (full attention matrix store). Flash Attention: tiling technique se attention compute karta hai bina full matrix store kiye. IO-aware algorithm - HBM aur SRAM ke beech data movement minimize karta hai. 2-4x faster, memory linear. Long sequences possible.
real_life_example: GPT-4 with 128K context: standard attention mein 128K × 128K matrix = 64GB memory sirf attention ke liye! Flash Attention se same computation fraction memory mein ho jaata hai. LLaMA, Mistral sab Flash Attention use karte hain production mein.
how_to_answer: Flash Attention: IO-aware exact attention algorithm
Standard attention: materializes full N×N attention matrix - O(N²) memory
Flash Attention: computes attention in blocks (tiling), O(N) memory
Key insight: minimize reads/writes between GPU HBM and SRAM
2-4x wall-clock speedup, significant memory savings
Enables longer context lengths in practice
Flash Attention 2: further optimizations for modern GPUs

question: What are adapter layers and how do they enable parameter-efficient fine-tuning?
hinglish_explanation: Full fine-tuning: sab parameters update (expensive for large models). Adapters: chhote trainable modules add karo between frozen layers. Sirf 1-5% parameters train karo, 95%+ frozen. Quality almost same. Multiple tasks ke liye different adapters, base model shared. LoRA bhi similar concept hai.
real_life_example: GPT-3 175B fine-tune karna = 175B parameters update = impossible for most. LoRA: sirf 0.1% parameters train karo (low-rank matrices), same quality. 100 different tasks ke liye 100 small LoRA adapters, ek shared base model. Cloud cost 100x kam!
how_to_answer: Adapters: small trainable modules inserted in frozen pre-trained model
Only adapter parameters trained (1-5% of total)
Original model weights remain frozen - no catastrophic forgetting
Multiple tasks: different adapters, shared base model
Adapter architecture: down-project → non-linearity → up-project
LoRA: low-rank decomposition of weight updates
Benefit: storage efficient, no forgetting, quick task switching

question: What is LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) and how does it work?
hinglish_explanation: LoRA key insight: fine-tuning mein weight changes low-rank hote hain. ΔW = A × B jahan A (d×r), B (r×d), r << d (rank 4-64). Sirf A aur B train karo, original W freeze. BERT-base mein 110M mein se sirf 0.3M parameters train! Inference mein merge kardo: W_new = W + A×B.
real_life_example: LLaMA-7B fine-tune: full = 7B params (28GB memory). LoRA rank=8: 4M params (16MB). Single GPU pe possible! Inference mein A×B merge karke original model size hi rehta hai - no extra latency. QLoRA: 4-bit quantized model + LoRA = 7B model on 6GB GPU!
how_to_answer: LoRA: approximate weight updates with low-rank matrices
ΔW = A × B where A is d×r, B is r×d, rank r << d
Only train A and B (tiny), freeze original W
Rank r=4-64 sufficient for most tasks
At inference: merge W + AB = no additional latency
Memory efficient: train large models on consumer GPUs
QLoRA: combine with quantization for extreme efficiency

question: What is the tokenizer's special tokens and their purpose?
hinglish_explanation: Special tokens model ko task structure batate hain. [CLS]: classification token (BERT). [SEP]: sentence boundary. [MASK]: MLM ke liye. [PAD]: padding. [BOS]/[EOS]: beginning/end of sequence (GPT). <s>, </s>: sentence markers. Har model ke apne special tokens hain.
real_life_example: BERT input: '[CLS] I love NLP [SEP] It is great [SEP]'. Classification: [CLS] ka embedding use karo. GPT: '<|endoftext|>' generation stop signal. ChatGPT: '<|im_start|>user\n...<|im_end|>' conversation structure.
how_to_answer: [CLS]: aggregate representation for classification (BERT)
[SEP]: separates sentence pairs in input
[MASK]: placeholder for masked language modeling
[PAD]: padding token for batch processing
[BOS]/[EOS] or <s>/</s>: sequence boundaries
[UNK]: unknown token (subword tokenizers rarely need it)
Model-specific: always check tokenizer documentation

question: What is the Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture in Transformers?
hinglish_explanation: MoE: FFN layer ko multiple expert networks mein split karo. Router/gating network decide karta hai kaunse experts activate honge (typically top-2). Total parameters bahut but computation per token limited. GPT-4 rumored MoE hai. Mixtral (Mistral) openly MoE hai - 47B params but 12B active per token.
real_life_example: Mixtral 8x7B: 8 experts each 7B, total 47B params but sirf 2 experts active per token = 12B computation. Quality 70B dense model ke comparable at fraction of compute! Switch Transformer (Google): 1.6T params with MoE. Cost-effective scaling.
how_to_answer: MoE: multiple expert FFN networks with learned routing
Router/gate: selects top-k experts for each token (k=1-2)
Sparse activation: only subset of parameters used per input
Total params large but compute per token limited
Benefits: scale model size without proportional compute increase
Challenges: load balancing, training instability, communication
Examples: Mixtral 8x7B, Switch Transformer, GPT-4 (rumored)

question: What is the context window limitation and how are models extending it?
hinglish_explanation: Transformer attention O(n²) hai - context length limit karta hai. BERT: 512 tokens, GPT-3: 2K, GPT-4: 128K, Claude: 200K. Extension methods: RoPE interpolation, ALiBi, FlashAttention memory savings, sparse attention patterns. Long context critical for: book summarization, code understanding, RAG.
real_life_example: Legal contract analysis: 100-page document = 30K+ tokens. GPT-3 (2K) nahi kar sakta. GPT-4-128K easily handles. Tricks: RoPE scaling (LLaMA 4K→32K extended), YaRN, position interpolation. Cost: longer context = more memory + compute.
how_to_answer: Context window: maximum tokens model can process at once
Limitation: self-attention O(n²) in compute and memory
Extension methods: RoPE interpolation, ALiBi, FlashAttention
Sparse attention: Longformer, BigBird handle 4K-16K tokens
Position interpolation: extend RoPE to longer sequences
Current models: GPT-4 128K, Claude 200K, Gemini 1M+
Tradeoff: longer context = more cost, potential quality degradation

question: What is the difference between pre-training, fine-tuning, and instruction tuning?
hinglish_explanation: Pre-training: large unlabeled data pe self-supervised (MLM/CLM). Fine-tuning: specific task pe labeled data se train. Instruction tuning: diverse instructions follow karna seekhna (FLAN, InstructGPT). RLHF: human preference se align karna. Pipeline: pre-train → instruction tune → RLHF → deploy.
real_life_example: GPT-4 pipeline: (1) Pre-train on internet text (predict next word). (2) Instruction tune: follow diverse instructions. (3) RLHF: human raters prefer which response. Result: helpful, harmless, honest assistant. Without instruction tuning, model just completes text randomly.
how_to_answer: Pre-training: self-supervised on large unlabeled corpus (MLM/CLM)
Fine-tuning: supervised on task-specific labeled data
Instruction tuning: train to follow diverse instructions (FLAN-style)
RLHF: align with human preferences using reward model
Pre-training: learns language; Instruction tuning: learns to follow directions
Full pipeline: pre-train → SFT (instruction) → RLHF → deployment
Each stage serves different purpose in model development

question: What is the residual connection in Transformers and why is it critical?
hinglish_explanation: Residual/skip connection: output = layer(x) + x. Input directly output mein add hota hai. Deep networks mein gradient directly flow kar sakta hai skip connection through. Without residuals: 12+ layer transformer train nahi hoga (vanishing gradients). Almost all deep architectures use karte hain.
real_life_example: BERT 12 layers deep hai. Residual connections ke bina layer 1 ka gradient layer 12 se back-propagate nahi ho paata effectively. ResNet (vision) ne introduce kiya, Transformer ne adopt kiya. Simple addition but critical for deep model training.
how_to_answer: Residual connection: output = sublayer(x) + x (skip connection)
Enables gradient flow through deep networks
Without: deep transformers (12+ layers) fail to train
Applied after each sub-layer: attention and FFN
Combined with layer normalization for stability
Allows each layer to learn residual/delta instead of full transformation
Inspired by ResNet, essential in all modern architectures

question: What is Grouped Query Attention (GQA) and Multi-Query Attention (MQA)?
hinglish_explanation: Standard: har head ke apne Q, K, V. MQA: sab heads share ek K, V (queries alag). GQA: groups of heads share K, V (middle ground). KV-cache memory reduce hota hai significantly. LLaMA-2 70B GQA use karta hai. Inference speed improve without much quality loss.
real_life_example: LLaMA-2 70B with 64 heads: MHA = 64 KV sets cached. GQA (8 groups) = 8 KV sets cached = 8x less KV-cache memory! Longer sequences serve ho sakti hain same GPU pe. Production serving ke liye critical optimization. Mistral bhi GQA use karta hai.
how_to_answer: MHA: each head has unique Q, K, V projections
MQA: all heads share single K, V; only Q is per-head
GQA: groups of heads share K, V (between MHA and MQA)
Benefit: reduces KV-cache memory during inference
MQA: most memory efficient but slight quality drop
GQA: good tradeoff between quality and efficiency
Used by: LLaMA-2 (GQA), PaLM (MQA), Mistral (GQA)

question: What is the Hugging Face Transformers library and how is it used?
hinglish_explanation: Hugging Face = NLP ka GitHub. Transformers library: pre-trained models load karo 2 lines mein, fine-tune karo easily. Model Hub pe 100K+ models available. Pipeline API: sentiment, NER, translation ek line mein. AutoModel/AutoTokenizer: correct model automatically load. Industry standard ban gaya hai.
real_life_example: Sentiment analysis 3 lines mein: from transformers import pipeline; classifier = pipeline('sentiment-analysis'); result = classifier('I love this product'). That's it! Production: model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased'); fine-tune on your data.
how_to_answer: HuggingFace Transformers: most popular NLP library
Model Hub: 100K+ pre-trained models available
Pipeline API: quick inference in one line for common tasks
AutoModel/AutoTokenizer: auto-detect correct model class
Trainer API: simplified fine-tuning with best practices
PEFT library: LoRA and adapter fine-tuning support
Integration: PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX export for deployment

question: What is the difference between absolute and relative positional encodings?
hinglish_explanation: Absolute: har position ko fixed embedding (sin/cos ya learned). Position 5 hamesha same embedding. Relative: positions ke beech ka distance encode karo (position 5 se position 3 = -2). Relative better generalize karta hai unseen lengths pe. T5, ALiBi, RoPE sab relative variants hain.
real_life_example: BERT: absolute positions (max 512). Input 513th token = crash. Relative positions (T5-style): koi fixed max nahi theoretically. RoPE (LLaMA): rotation-based relative - 4K pe train karo but position interpolation se 32K pe inference possible.
how_to_answer: Absolute: each position gets fixed/learned embedding
Relative: encode distance between positions, not absolute position
Absolute: cannot generalize to unseen sequence lengths
Relative: better length generalization (extrapolation)
T5: learned relative position bias added to attention scores
RoPE: rotary encoding, encodes relative position in attention
ALiBi: simple linear bias based on distance, no position embeddings

question: What is model quantization for Transformers?
hinglish_explanation: Quantization: FP32 weights ko INT8/INT4 mein convert karna. Model 4x-8x chhota ho jaata hai, inference faster. Minimal quality loss (1-2%). GPTQ, AWQ, bitsandbytes popular methods hain. 7B model: FP32=28GB, FP16=14GB, INT8=7GB, INT4=3.5GB. Consumer GPU pe LLM possible!
real_life_example: LLaMA-7B: FP16 mein 14GB VRAM chahiye (RTX 3090 barely fit). 4-bit quantize: 3.5GB (RTX 3060 pe run!). Quality: 90-95% retained. QLoRA: 4-bit quantized model pe LoRA fine-tuning = cheapest way to customize LLM. ollama locally quantized models run karta hai.
how_to_answer: Quantization: reduce precision of model weights (FP32→INT8/INT4)
Benefits: smaller model, faster inference, less memory
Methods: post-training quantization (PTQ), quantization-aware training (QAT)
Popular: GPTQ (GPU), AWQ (activation-aware), bitsandbytes (easy)
4-bit: 8x compression with ~5% quality loss
Enables LLMs on consumer hardware (laptops, phones)
Combine with KV-cache optimization for efficient serving

question: What is the scaling law for language models?
hinglish_explanation: Scaling laws (Kaplan et al.): model performance smoothly improves with more parameters, data, and compute following power laws. Loss ∝ N^(-0.076) for params. Chinchilla finding: optimal training = 20 tokens per parameter. 7B model needs 140B tokens. Guides how much to invest in model size vs data.
real_life_example: GPT-3 (175B params) trained on 300B tokens = over-parameterized. Chinchilla (70B params) trained on 1.4T tokens = same compute, better quality! LLaMA followed Chinchilla: 7B trained on 1T+ tokens. Scaling laws predict performance before expensive training runs.
how_to_answer: Scaling laws: predictable relationship between compute/data/params and loss
Loss decreases as power law with increasing model size, data, compute
Kaplan (OpenAI): scale model size more than data
Chinchilla (DeepMind): optimal ratio ~20 tokens per parameter
Practical: predict model performance before full training
Emergent abilities: some capabilities appear only at certain scales
Used to: plan compute budgets, predict ROI of scaling

question: What is the difference between encoder and decoder self-attention?
hinglish_explanation: Encoder self-attention: bidirectional - har token sab tokens dekh sakta hai (BERT). Decoder self-attention: causal - har token sirf previous tokens dekh sakta hai (GPT). Cross-attention (encoder-decoder): decoder encoder ke outputs attend karta hai. Three distinct attention types in full Transformer.
real_life_example: Translation: Encoder 'I love India' bidirectionally encode karta hai. Decoder 'मुझे भारत पसंद है' generate karte waqt: (1) causal self-attention previous Hindi words pe, (2) cross-attention English encoder output pe. Teen alag attention mechanisms ek model mein.
how_to_answer: Encoder self-attention: bidirectional, sees all tokens (no mask)
Decoder self-attention: causal mask, sees only past tokens
Cross-attention: decoder queries attend to encoder keys/values
Encoder: understanding (BERT uses this only)
Decoder: generation (GPT uses causal self-attention only)
Full Transformer: all three types (T5 encoder-decoder)
Mask difference: encoder=no mask, decoder=causal triangular mask

question: What is machine translation and what are modern approaches?
hinglish_explanation: Ek language se dusri language mein text convert karna. Evolution: rule-based → statistical (phrase-based) → neural (seq2seq+attention) → Transformer. Google Translate ab Transformer use karta hai. mBART, mT5 multilingual models 100+ languages handle karte hain. Low-resource languages ke liye transfer learning critical hai.
real_life_example: Google Translate: English→Hindi daily millions use karte hain. Quality 2016 mein dramatically improve hui jab Google ne NMT (Neural MT) switch kiya. Indian languages: IndicTrans2 by AI4Bharat 22 Indian languages support karta hai BART architecture pe.
how_to_answer: Convert text from source language to target language
Evolution: rule-based → statistical → neural (2014+) → transformer
Modern: encoder-decoder transformers (mBART, mT5, NLLB)
Training: parallel corpus (aligned sentence pairs)
Challenges: low-resource languages, domain adaptation, idioms
Evaluation: BLEU, chrF, COMET (human-correlated metrics)
Indian languages: IndicTrans2, Google Translate, Microsoft Translator

question: What is text summarization? Explain extractive vs abstractive approaches.
hinglish_explanation: Long text ka short summary banana. Extractive: original se important sentences select karo (copy-paste). Abstractive: apne words mein nayi summary generate karo (paraphrase). Extractive safe hai but robotic. Abstractive natural but hallucination risk. Modern: BART/T5 abstractive SOTA hain.
real_life_example: News app: 500 word article ka 50 word summary. Extractive: top 2 sentences pick karo (TextRank). Abstractive: BART/Pegasus se natural summary generate karo. inshorts app 60-word news summaries - mix of extractive selection + abstractive rewriting.
how_to_answer: Text summarization: condense long text preserving key information
Extractive: select important sentences from original (no new words)
Abstractive: generate new sentences capturing key points
Extractive methods: TextRank, LexRank, BertSum
Abstractive methods: BART, Pegasus, T5 (encoder-decoder models)
Hybrid: extract key sentences, then paraphrase them
Evaluation: ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, BERTScore

question: What is question answering (QA) and what types exist?
hinglish_explanation: Question ka answer dena - either extract from context (extractive QA) ya generate (generative QA). Types: reading comprehension (answer in passage), open-domain (any question), knowledge-based (structured KB). SQuAD benchmark famous hai. BERT span extraction se karta hai - start/end position predict.
real_life_example: Google Search featured snippets: question ka direct answer dikhata hai. 'Who is PM of India?' → 'Narendra Modi' extract from webpage. Banking chatbot: 'What is my balance?' → retrieves from database. RAG: retrieve relevant docs + generate answer.
how_to_answer: QA: automatically answer questions in natural language
Extractive: identify answer span in given context (SQuAD-style)
Generative: generate answer text (may not be in context)
Open-domain: no context given, must retrieve relevant documents
Knowledge-based: query structured knowledge graphs
BERT for extractive: predict start and end positions of answer
Modern: RAG combines retrieval + generation for best results

question: What is reading comprehension and how do models solve it?
hinglish_explanation: Passage diya + question pucha = answer passage mein dhundho. SQuAD: 100K+ question-answer pairs from Wikipedia. BERT approach: passage+question input, har token ke liye start/end probability predict. Answer = span with highest start×end probability. Unanswerable questions bhi handle karna padta hai.
real_life_example: UPSC preparation: passage padhke questions answer karna - exactly what reading comprehension models karte hain! EduTech apps mein: passage dedo, model automatically questions ke answers extract karega. Exam auto-grading mein use hota hai.
how_to_answer: Given passage + question, find/generate the answer
SQuAD dataset: 100K+ examples, Wikipedia passages
BERT approach: predict start and end positions of answer span
Input: [CLS] question [SEP] passage [SEP]
Output: probability of each token being start/end of answer
Handle unanswerable: if no-answer score > threshold, output 'N/A'
Modern: LLMs do reading comprehension as part of general capability

question: What is text generation and what are the key challenges?
hinglish_explanation: Model se natural text produce karana - stories, articles, code, emails. Challenges: repetition (same phrase baar baar), hallucination (galat facts), coherence (topic drift), diversity (boring/generic outputs). Decoding strategy critical: temperature, top-p, repetition penalty control quality.
real_life_example: ChatGPT: conversation generate karta hai. GitHub Copilot: code generate. Jasper AI: marketing copy. Challenges real hain: ChatGPT confident lagta hai wrong facts pe (hallucination). Same prompt pe same reply (low diversity). Long text mein topic drift.
how_to_answer: Generate fluent, coherent natural language text
Approaches: autoregressive (GPT), encoder-decoder (T5)
Challenges: repetition, hallucination, coherence, diversity
Repetition: repetition penalty, n-gram blocking
Hallucination: RAG for grounded generation, fact verification
Decoding: temperature, top-k, top-p, beam search
Evaluation: perplexity (auto), human eval for quality

question: What are dialogue systems and how are they built?
hinglish_explanation: Conversational AI - multi-turn interactions handle karna. Types: task-oriented (Ola booking) aur open-domain (ChatGPT). Components: NLU (intent+entities), dialogue manager (state tracking), NLG (response). Modern: end-to-end LLMs with instruction tuning. Context maintenance across turns critical.
real_life_example: Ola/Uber chatbot (task-oriented): intent detect (book ride), entities extract (from, to, time), slot filling, API call, response generate. ChatGPT (open-domain): general conversation koi bhi topic pe. Banking IVR: voice-based dialogue system for account queries.
how_to_answer: Dialogue systems: conversational AI for multi-turn interaction
Task-oriented: specific goal (booking, customer service), slot filling
Open-domain: general conversation, no specific goal
Traditional pipeline: NLU → Dialogue State Tracking → Policy → NLG
Modern: end-to-end with LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude)
Key challenge: maintaining context across multiple turns
Evaluation: task success rate, user satisfaction, dialogue length

question: What is relation extraction in NLP?
hinglish_explanation: Text mein entities ke beech relationships identify karna. 'Sundar Pichai is CEO of Google' → (Sundar Pichai, CEO-of, Google). Knowledge graph building ka foundation hai. Approaches: pattern-based, supervised classification, distant supervision (Freebase se auto-label). Modern: prompt-based extraction with LLMs.
real_life_example: News: 'Mukesh Ambani acquired Hamleys for $67M' → (Mukesh Ambani, acquired, Hamleys), (acquisition, amount, $67M). Automatically knowledge graphs build karte hain companies ke relationships track karne ke liye. Investment firms ye use karte hain market intelligence ke liye.
how_to_answer: Identify semantic relationships between entities in text
Output: (subject, relation, object) triples
Relation types: works-at, located-in, founded-by, etc.
Approaches: supervised, distant supervision, few-shot with LLMs
Distant supervision: use KB to auto-generate training data
Pipeline: NER first, then classify relation between entity pairs
Applications: knowledge graph construction, information extraction

question: What is coreference resolution?
hinglish_explanation: Text mein same entity ke different mentions ko link karna. 'Virat scored a century. He was overjoyed. The captain raised his bat.' - 'Virat', 'He', 'The captain', 'his' sab same person refer karte hain. Document understanding ke liye essential hai. Modern: SpanBERT-based models best hain.
real_life_example: Legal document: 'The Plaintiff filed a case. She claimed damages.' - 'She' = 'Plaintiff' link karna padega automated analysis ke liye. Chatbot context: user 'I ordered a phone' then 'when will it arrive' - 'it' = 'phone' samajhna padega.
how_to_answer: Link all mentions that refer to same entity in text
Mentions: pronouns, names, descriptions referring to same entity
Example: [John] went home. [He] was tired. → He=John
Approaches: rule-based (Hobbs), ML-based, neural (end-to-end)
Modern: SpanBERT + span-pair scoring (Lee et al.)
Challenges: long-distance references, world knowledge needed
Applications: text understanding, summarization, QA, dialogue

question: What is semantic role labeling (SRL)?
hinglish_explanation: Sentence mein WHO did WHAT to WHOM, WHERE, WHEN identify karna. 'Ram gave Sita a book in Delhi yesterday' → Agent:Ram, Action:gave, Recipient:Sita, Theme:book, Location:Delhi, Time:yesterday. Predicate-argument structure extract karta hai. Deep understanding of events.
real_life_example: News analysis: 'The government increased fuel prices by 5% effective Monday' → Agent:government, Action:increased, Theme:fuel prices, Extent:5%, Time:Monday. Automated event extraction aur knowledge base population ke liye critical hai.
how_to_answer: SRL: identify semantic roles of arguments around predicates
Who did what to whom, where, when, why, how
Roles: Agent, Patient, Theme, Instrument, Location, Time
PropBank-style: ARG0 (agent), ARG1 (patient), ARGM (modifiers)
Approaches: BiLSTM-CRF, BERT-based span classification
Related to: dependency parsing, frame semantics
Applications: event extraction, QA, information extraction

question: What is dependency parsing?
hinglish_explanation: Sentence mein words ke grammatical relationships (dependencies) identify karna. 'The cat sat on the mat' → sat←(nsubj)←cat, sat→(prep)→on→(pobj)→mat. Tree structure banti hai jahan root usually main verb hota hai. SpaCy dependency parsing support karta hai. Information extraction ke liye useful.
real_life_example: 'Reserve Bank of India increased repo rate' - dependency parse bataega ki 'Reserve Bank of India' ek noun phrase hai (subject), 'increased' main verb, 'repo rate' object. Automated question generation mein use hota hai - subject/object swap karke questions banao.
how_to_answer: Parse grammatical dependencies between words in sentence
Output: tree with labeled edges (nsubj, dobj, prep, etc.)
Each word has exactly one head (parent) except root
Types: projective and non-projective trees
Approaches: transition-based (fast), graph-based (accurate)
Universal Dependencies: cross-lingual dependency framework
Tools: SpaCy, Stanza, Stanford Parser - fast and accurate

question: What is constituency parsing and how does it differ from dependency parsing?
hinglish_explanation: Constituency: sentence ko nested phrases (NP, VP, PP) mein break karo - hierarchical tree. 'The big cat' = NP(DET('The') ADJ('big') N('cat')). Dependency: words ke beech direct relationships. Constituency structure dikhata hai, dependency function dikhata hai. Modern NLP mein dependency zyada popular hai.
real_life_example: Grammar checking: constituency tree se phrase structure errors detect hote hain. 'The went store' → NP incomplete (no noun after 'The'). Machine translation mein reordering constituency tree pe based hoti thi historically.
how_to_answer: Constituency: break sentence into nested phrases (NP, VP, PP, S)
Dependency: direct relationships between individual words
Constituency: phrase structure tree (top-down bracketing)
Dependency: labeled directed graph of word-word relations
Constituency: good for phrase-level operations, reordering
Dependency: good for semantic relations, information extraction
Modern preference: dependency parsing (simpler, cross-lingual)

question: What is information extraction (IE) and what are its components?
hinglish_explanation: Unstructured text se structured information nikalna. Components: NER (entities), RE (relations), event extraction (events), temporal extraction (dates/times). Raw news articles se automatically facts extract → database/knowledge graph. Foundation of many NLP applications hai.
real_life_example: Job portal: resume se automatically extract: Name, Skills, Experience, Education, Companies. Structured format mein store. News monitoring: articles se automatically company acquisitions, leadership changes, funding rounds extract karo for investors.
how_to_answer: IE: extract structured information from unstructured text
Components: NER, Relation Extraction, Event Extraction
NER: identify entities (person, org, location, date)
RE: identify relationships between entities
Event extraction: who did what, when, where
Output: structured data (tables, knowledge graphs, databases)
Applications: resume parsing, news monitoring, scientific literature mining

question: What is Natural Language Inference (NLI)?
hinglish_explanation: Do sentences ka relationship determine karna: entailment (supports), contradiction (opposes), neutral (unrelated). Premise: 'A man is playing guitar'. Hypothesis: 'A musician is performing' → entailment. NLI models text understanding test karte hain. SNLI, MultiNLI datasets famous hain.
real_life_example: Fact verification: Claim 'India won 2023 Cricket World Cup' vs evidence 'Australia won the 2023 ODI World Cup Final against India' → contradiction. Fake news detection mein NLI use hota hai - claim vs evidence compare.
how_to_answer: NLI: determine relationship between premise and hypothesis
Three classes: entailment, contradiction, neutral
Entailment: hypothesis follows from premise
Contradiction: hypothesis conflicts with premise
Neutral: no clear relationship
Datasets: SNLI (570K), MultiNLI (433K), XNLI (multilingual)
Used for: zero-shot classification, fact verification, QA

question: What is abstractive summarization and how does Pegasus work?
hinglish_explanation: Abstractive summarization apne words mein nayi summary generate karta hai - sirf copy nahi. Pegasus: pre-training mein important sentences mask karta hai (Gap Sentence Generation) aur model unhe generate karna seekhta hai. Summarization-specific pre-training = better summaries. News summarization mein SOTA tha.
real_life_example: News article: 500 words about RBI policy decision → Pegasus generates: 'RBI maintained repo rate at 6.5% citing inflation concerns while revising GDP growth forecast upward to 7%'. Original mein exact ye sentence nahi hai - model ne synthesize kiya.
how_to_answer: Abstractive: generate new text capturing key points (not just extract)
Pegasus: pre-training designed specifically for summarization
GSG (Gap Sentence Generation): mask important sentences, predict them
Importance: select sentences similar to rest of document (pseudo-summaries)
Architecture: encoder-decoder Transformer
SOTA on 12 summarization benchmarks with minimal fine-tuning
Other models: BART, T5, LED (long documents)

question: What is intent classification and slot filling in dialogue systems?
hinglish_explanation: Intent: user kya karna chahta hai (book_flight, check_weather, play_music). Slot filling: important details extract (destination=Mumbai, date=tomorrow). Jointly karna padta hai - BERT-based joint models best hain. Chatbot/voice assistant ka core NLU component hai.
real_life_example: 'Book a flight to Mumbai tomorrow for 2 people' → Intent: book_flight, Slots: {destination: Mumbai, date: tomorrow, passengers: 2}. Alexa/Siri mein har utterance pe ye processing hoti hai. MakeMyTrip chatbot exactly ye karta hai.
how_to_answer: Intent: classify user's goal (what they want to do)
Slot filling: extract relevant parameters (NER-like)
Joint modeling: predict intent and slots simultaneously
BERT-based: [CLS] for intent, token-level for slots
Few-shot: use LLMs with examples for new intents/slots
Datasets: ATIS, SNIPS, MultiWOZ for benchmarking
Production: combine with dialogue state tracking for multi-turn

question: What is text-to-SQL and how does it work?
hinglish_explanation: Natural language question ko SQL query mein convert karna. 'Show me all orders above 10000 from last month' → SELECT * FROM orders WHERE amount > 10000 AND date >= '2024-01-01'. Schema-aware models table structure samajhte hain. LLMs ke saath few-shot prompting se bhi kaam karta hai.
real_life_example: Business users jo SQL nahi jaante: 'Last quarter mein sabse zyada revenue kaunse city se aayi?' → SQL automatically generate. Metabase, ThoughtSpot jaise tools ye internally use karte hain. Data democratization - anyone can query databases!
how_to_answer: Convert natural language questions to SQL queries
Input: question + database schema (tables, columns)
Output: executable SQL query
Approaches: seq2seq, grammar-based, LLM prompting
Schema linking: map question words to schema elements
Challenges: complex joins, nested queries, ambiguity
Benchmarks: Spider (cross-database), WikiSQL (simple)

question: What is event extraction in NLP?
hinglish_explanation: Text se events identify karna: kya hua (trigger), kisne kiya (agent), kisko hua (patient), kab, kahan. 'Terrorist attack killed 5 people in Mumbai yesterday' → Event: Attack, Victims: 5, Location: Mumbai, Time: yesterday. News analysis aur intelligence ke liye critical.
real_life_example: Financial news monitoring: 'Infosys acquired company X for $100M' → Event: Acquisition, Buyer: Infosys, Target: X, Amount: $100M. Automated trading systems use event extraction - acquisition announcement = stock price movement prediction.
how_to_answer: Extract structured event information from text
Event components: trigger (verb/noun), arguments (who, what, when, where)
Types: ACE events (attack, movement, transaction, etc.)
Approaches: pipeline (trigger → arguments) or joint extraction
Modern: prompt-based extraction with LLMs
Challenges: nested events, implicit events, cross-sentence events
Applications: intelligence analysis, financial news, crisis monitoring

question: What is keyword extraction and what algorithms are used?
hinglish_explanation: Document se important words/phrases automatically extract karna. Statistical: TF-IDF top terms. Graph-based: TextRank (words as nodes, co-occurrence as edges, PageRank). ML-based: KeyBERT (BERT embeddings + cosine similarity with document). SEO, tagging, summarization mein use hota hai.
real_life_example: Blog post se automatic tags generate: article about 'machine learning in healthcare' → keywords: 'machine learning', 'healthcare AI', 'diagnosis prediction'. KeyBERT: document embedding se closest word/phrase embeddings = keywords. Hashnode/Medium auto-tags aise hi generate hote hain.
how_to_answer: Extract most representative words/phrases from document
Statistical: TF-IDF based term importance
Graph-based: TextRank, RAKE (Rapid Automatic Keyword Extraction)
Embedding-based: KeyBERT (cosine similarity to document)
YAKE: unsupervised, no training needed, multi-lingual
Evaluation: precision, recall vs human-annotated keywords
Use cases: SEO, document tagging, search indexing, summarization

question: What is aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA)?
hinglish_explanation: Simple sentiment (pos/neg) ke bajaye, specific aspects ke liye alag sentiment. Restaurant review: 'Food was great but service was slow' → food: positive, service: negative. Three subtasks: aspect extraction, aspect categorization, sentiment for each aspect. Fine-grained analysis for businesses.
real_life_example: Zomato reviews analysis: 'Butter chicken amazing, ambiance romantic, but waiting time 45 min!' → food:positive, ambiance:positive, service:negative. Restaurant owner ko pata chalega ki specifically service fix karna hai. Product reviews pe Amazon bhi ABSA use karta hai.
how_to_answer: ABSA: determine sentiment toward specific aspects/features
Subtasks: aspect term extraction, categorization, polarity classification
Example: 'Great battery but camera is poor' → battery:pos, camera:neg
Approaches: rule-based, attention-based neural, BERT fine-tuning
Datasets: SemEval restaurant/laptop reviews, SentiHood
Joint models: extract aspects and predict sentiment simultaneously
Business value: actionable insights from customer feedback

question: What is text clustering and how is it applied?
hinglish_explanation: Similar documents ko groups mein organize karna without predefined labels (unsupervised). Process: text→embeddings→clustering algorithm (K-Means, HDBSCAN). Topic discovery, duplicate detection, content organization. SBERT embeddings + HDBSCAN popular modern approach hai.
real_life_example: Customer support: 10K unorganized tickets cluster karo → automatically topics discover: 'payment issues', 'delivery complaints', 'app crashes'. Priority aur routing automatically possible. BERTopic: SBERT + HDBSCAN + TF-IDF representation = excellent topic clusters.
how_to_answer: Group similar documents without predefined categories (unsupervised)
Pipeline: text → embedding → dimensionality reduction → clustering
Embeddings: TF-IDF (traditional), SBERT (modern)
Algorithms: K-Means, DBSCAN, HDBSCAN, Agglomerative
BERTopic: SBERT + UMAP + HDBSCAN + c-TF-IDF (SOTA)
Challenges: determining optimal number of clusters, evaluation
Applications: topic discovery, content organization, deduplication

question: What is cross-lingual transfer learning?
hinglish_explanation: Ek language ke data pe train karo, dusri language pe use karo. mBERT/XLM-R multilingual models hain jo 100+ languages ka shared embedding space learn karte hain. English training data → zero-shot Hindi inference possible! Low-resource Indian languages ke liye game-changer hai.
real_life_example: English mein 100K labeled sentiment data available. Hindi mein sirf 500. Cross-lingual: XLM-R English pe train karo, Hindi pe test karo - 85%+ accuracy without any Hindi training data! IndicBERT specifically Indian languages ke liye trained hai.
how_to_answer: Train on one language, apply to another without target language data
Multilingual models: mBERT, XLM-R share embedding space across languages
Zero-shot transfer: fine-tune on English, evaluate on Hindi
Translate-train: translate training data to target language
Approaches: shared vocabulary, language-agnostic representations
Works best for: similar languages, well-represented in pre-training
Indian languages: IndicBERT, MuRIL (Google) optimized for India

question: What is named entity linking (NEL) and how does it differ from NER?
hinglish_explanation: NER: text mein 'Apple' entity identify karo (ORG). NEL: us entity ko knowledge base mein link karo - kaunsa Apple? Apple Inc. (Q312) ya Apple fruit? Disambiguation + linking. Wikipedia/Wikidata mein entity match karna. Entity disambiguation crucial step hai.
real_life_example: 'Sachin scored a century' - NER: Sachin = PERSON. NEL: kaunsa Sachin? Sachin Tendulkar (cricketer) ya Sachin Pilot (politician)? Context se decide karo 'scored century' → Sachin Tendulkar (Wikidata Q9488). Google Knowledge Panel ye use karta hai.
how_to_answer: NEL: link entity mentions to knowledge base entries
NER: identify entity type; NEL: disambiguate and link to KB
Steps: mention detection → candidate generation → entity disambiguation
Candidate generation: find possible KB entities for mention
Disambiguation: use context to select correct entity
Knowledge bases: Wikipedia, Wikidata, Freebase
Applications: knowledge graph population, semantic search, QA

question: What is text paraphrasing and what are its applications?
hinglish_explanation: Same meaning ko different words mein express karna. 'The cat is on the mat' → 'A feline is sitting on the rug'. Applications: data augmentation (training data badhao), plagiarism detection, query expansion, simplification. T5/GPT-based models paraphrasing well karte hain.
real_life_example: Data augmentation: sirf 100 intent examples hain. Paraphrase karke 500 banao - model better generalize karega. Plagiarism check: student ne paraphrase kiya hai ya copy-paste? Semantic similarity se detect karo. Grammarly sentence rephrasing feature.
how_to_answer: Rewrite text preserving meaning with different words/structure
Applications: data augmentation, plagiarism detection, simplification
Methods: rule-based (synonym replacement), neural (T5, GPT, BART)
Back-translation: translate to other language and back
Evaluation: semantic similarity (BERTScore) + lexical diversity
PAWS dataset: paraphrase identification benchmark
Quality: meaning preservation + surface form diversity

question: What is document-level NLP and why is it harder than sentence-level?
hinglish_explanation: Sentence-level: ek sentence independently process. Document-level: pura document context chahiye - coreference across sentences, discourse structure, document-level sentiment. Long-range dependencies, coherence, topic transitions sab handle karna padta hai. Models ko longer context chahiye.
real_life_example: Movie review: first paragraph positive, middle neutral, last paragraph 'but overall disappointing'. Document-level sentiment = negative (conclusion matters). Sentence-level: 3 positive, 2 neutral, 1 negative → majority vote misleading! Document structure matters.
how_to_answer: Document-level: process entire document considering cross-sentence context
Challenges: long-range dependencies, coreference, discourse structure
Sentence-level: each sentence independent, no cross-sentence reasoning
Document tasks: summarization, document classification, entity linking
Models: Longformer, BigBird, LED for long documents
Hierarchical: sentence embeddings → document embedding approach
Key insight: document meaning ≠ sum of sentence meanings

question: What is data augmentation for NLP tasks?
hinglish_explanation: Training data artificially badhana without manual labeling. Techniques: synonym replacement, random insertion/deletion, back-translation, paraphrasing, contextual augmentation (BERT fill mask). Low-resource scenarios mein 5-15% accuracy improve kar sakta hai. But careful: augmented data quality matter karta hai.
real_life_example: Intent classification: sirf 50 examples per intent. Augmentation: 'Book a flight to Delhi' → 'Reserve a flight to Delhi' (synonym), 'Book a flight to Mumbai' (entity swap), 'I want to book flight to Delhi' (paraphrase). 50→200 examples without manual effort.
how_to_answer: Artificially expand training data for better generalization
Techniques: synonym replacement, back-translation, paraphrase
EDA (Easy Data Augmentation): random insert/swap/delete words
Back-translation: English→Hindi→English gives paraphrases
Contextual: BERT mask-and-fill for diverse substitutions
Label-preserving: ensure augmented text keeps same label
Most effective for: low-resource (< 1000 examples) settings

question: What is discourse analysis and how does it relate to NLP?
hinglish_explanation: Discourse: sentences ke beech relationships aur text ka overall structure. Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST): sentences ke beech relations (cause, contrast, elaboration). Coherence: text logically connected hai ya nahi. Essay scoring, summarization, argumentation mining mein use hota hai.
real_life_example: Essay grading: well-structured essay mein clear introduction → arguments → conclusion flow. Discourse analysis detect karta hai ki essay coherent hai ya random sentences. Automated essay scoring systems (ETS, Turnitin) discourse features use karte hain.
how_to_answer: Discourse: how sentences relate to form coherent text
RST (Rhetorical Structure Theory): labeled tree of relations
Relations: cause, contrast, elaboration, condition, temporal
Coherence: logical flow between sentences
Applications: essay scoring, summarization, argumentation mining
Models: discourse parsers, BERT-based coherence scoring
Challenges: implicit relations, long-distance connections

question: What is zero-shot text classification and how does it work?
hinglish_explanation: Bina task-specific training ke classification karna. NLI-based approach: 'This text is about sports' hypothesis banakar entailment check karo. Candidate labels mein se highest entailment = predicted class. HuggingFace pipeline mein zero-shot-classification available hai. New categories add karna instant hai!
real_life_example: Content moderation: naya category 'cryptocurrency scam' detect karna hai. Traditional: labeled data collect karo, model train karo (weeks). Zero-shot: bas label name do 'cryptocurrency scam', NLI model turant classify karega. Instant deployment of new categories!
how_to_answer: Classify text into categories without task-specific training data
NLI-based: treat classification as textual entailment
For each label, create hypothesis: 'This text is about {label}'
Check entailment between text (premise) and hypothesis
Highest entailment score = predicted class
Models: bart-large-mnli, deberta-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli
Advantage: add new categories instantly without retraining

question: What is multi-task learning in NLP?
hinglish_explanation: Ek model multiple tasks simultaneously train karo - NER + POS + classification together. Shared encoder common features seekhta hai, task-specific heads alag predictions dete hain. T5 naturally multi-task hai (text-to-text). Benefits: regularization, knowledge sharing between related tasks, data efficiency.
real_life_example: SpaCy model: simultaneously POS tagging, NER, dependency parsing seekhta hai ek hi model mein. Google's BERT: fine-tune on multiple tasks improves each. MT-DNN: multi-task pre-training improves downstream. ChatGPT: one model handles translation, QA, summarization, coding - ultimate multi-task!
how_to_answer: Train single model on multiple tasks simultaneously
Shared representation: encoder learns general features
Task-specific heads: separate output layers per task
Benefits: regularization, knowledge transfer, data efficiency
Hard parameter sharing: common layers + task heads
Soft parameter sharing: separate models with regularization
Examples: T5 (text-to-text multi-task), MT-DNN, UniLM

question: What is textual entailment and how is it used for downstream tasks?
hinglish_explanation: Premise se hypothesis logically follow karta hai ya nahi. 'All birds can fly' (premise) → 'Sparrows can fly' (hypothesis) = entailment. Versatile format hai - classification, QA, fact-checking sab NLI format mein convert ho sakte hain. Universal task format ban gaya hai.
real_life_example: Fake news detection: news article (premise) vs claim (hypothesis) - entailment=true, contradiction=false. Product attribute extraction: 'Cotton shirt, blue color' entails 'Material: Cotton'? Sab problems NLI mein reformulate ho sakte hain.
how_to_answer: Textual entailment: does premise logically imply hypothesis?
Foundation for zero-shot classification, fact verification
Any classification → entailment: text=premise, 'This is {label}'=hypothesis
Models: DeBERTa-mnli, BART-mnli, RoBERTa-large-mnli
Training data: SNLI, MultiNLI, ANLI (adversarial)
Very versatile: many tasks can be cast as entailment
Part of Natural Language Inference (NLI) framework

question: What is open information extraction (OpenIE)?
hinglish_explanation: Traditional IE: predefined relations (works-at, born-in). OpenIE: ANY relation extract karo bina predefined schema ke. 'Einstein was born in Ulm' → (Einstein, was born in, Ulm). Schema-free, domain-independent. Challenges: noisy extractions, non-informative triples. Large-scale knowledge extraction ke liye useful.
real_life_example: Wikipedia articles se automatically knowledge base build: har sentence se (subject, relation, object) triples extract. '10 lakh articles → 50 lakh facts' automatically. Google Knowledge Graph initially OpenIE se partly built hua tha. Any new domain mein instantly applicable.
how_to_answer: Extract relations from text without predefined schema
Output: (arg1, relation phrase, arg2) triples
No fixed relation types: any verb phrase can be relation
Systems: ReVerb, OLLIE, Stanford OpenIE, OpenIE6
Advantages: domain-independent, scalable, no training data needed
Challenges: noisy extractions, uninformative triples, no normalization
Modern: LLM-based extraction with better quality and coverage

question: What are Large Language Models (LLMs) and what makes them different from previous models?
hinglish_explanation: LLMs: billions of parameters pe trained transformer models (GPT-4, LLaMA, Claude). Scale pe emergent abilities aati hain - reasoning, code generation, few-shot learning. Previous models: task-specific training needed. LLMs: one model, all tasks via prompting. Paradigm shift from fine-tuning to prompting.
real_life_example: GPT-3 (175B params) suddenly few-shot learning dikhane laga - 3 examples do prompt mein, nayi task seekh jaata hai. GPT-4: complex reasoning, multimodal (image+text), bar exam pass. India: Krutrim, Hanooman, BharatGPT developing Indian LLMs.
how_to_answer: LLMs: very large transformer models (billions of parameters)
Scale enables emergent abilities: reasoning, few-shot, instruction following
Key models: GPT-4, Claude, LLaMA, Gemini, Mistral
Paradigm shift: fine-tuning → prompting/in-context learning
Training: pre-training on internet-scale data + alignment (RLHF)
Capabilities: translation, code, math, reasoning, creative writing
Challenges: hallucination, cost, safety, bias

question: What is prompt engineering and why is it important?
hinglish_explanation: LLM se best output lene ke liye input (prompt) carefully design karna. Clear instructions, examples, format specification, role assignment - sab prompt engineering hai. Good prompt = accurate output. Bad prompt = garbage output. Same model, different prompts = dramatically different quality.
real_life_example: Bad prompt: 'Tell me about India'. Good prompt: 'You are a travel guide. List top 5 tourist destinations in India with best visiting month, budget estimate in INR, and one unique activity at each location. Format as table.' Night and day difference in output quality.
how_to_answer: Crafting effective inputs to get desired outputs from LLMs
Techniques: clear instructions, examples, format specification
Few-shot: provide examples in prompt for task demonstration
Chain-of-thought: ask model to reason step by step
Role prompting: 'You are an expert in X'
System prompts: set behavior and constraints
Iterative refinement: test and improve prompts systematically

question: What is in-context learning (ICL) and how does it work?
hinglish_explanation: Model ko prompt mein examples dedo, bina weight update ke nayi task seekh jaata hai. Zero-shot: koi example nahi. Few-shot: 3-5 examples. Model examples se pattern identify karta hai aur apply karta hai. GPT-3 ne ye capability demonstrate ki thi. Weight change nahi hota - sirf context se learn!
real_life_example: Sentiment classification without training: prompt mein 3 examples do: 'Great product → positive', 'Terrible service → negative', 'Okay quality → neutral'. Then: 'Amazing delivery → ?' Model 'positive' output karega. No fine-tuning, no gradient update. Just examples in context!
how_to_answer: ICL: learning from examples provided in the prompt without weight updates
Zero-shot: no examples, just instructions
One-shot: single example provided
Few-shot: 3-5 examples demonstrating the task
Model infers pattern from examples, applies to new input
No gradient update: purely from context/attention mechanism
Emergent at scale: appears in large models (>1B parameters)

question: What is Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and why does it improve reasoning?
hinglish_explanation: Model ko step-by-step reasoning karne ka instruction do instead of direct answer. 'Think step by step' add kardo = reasoning accuracy dramatically improve. Complex math, logic problems mein especially useful. Model intermediate steps generate karke better final answer deta hai. Zero-shot CoT: sirf 'Let's think step by step' add karo.
real_life_example: Without CoT: 'Roger has 5 balls, buys 2 cans of 3 balls each. Total?' → Model: '11' (wrong). With CoT: 'Think step by step' → Model: 'Roger starts with 5. Buys 2×3=6. Total=5+6=11' → correct! GSM8K math benchmark pe 50%→95% accuracy improvement with CoT.
how_to_answer: CoT: prompt model to show reasoning steps before final answer
Elicits step-by-step reasoning for complex problems
Few-shot CoT: provide examples with reasoning steps
Zero-shot CoT: just add 'Let's think step by step'
Dramatically improves: math, logic, multi-hop reasoning
Works because: intermediate tokens provide working memory
Limitation: can generate plausible-looking but wrong reasoning

question: What is RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and how does it work?
hinglish_explanation: RAG = Retrieve relevant documents + Generate answer using them. LLM ka knowledge outdated/limited hota hai. RAG: user question → vector search → relevant chunks retrieve → LLM ko context mein do → grounded answer. Hallucination reduce, up-to-date info, source attribution possible.
real_life_example: Company chatbot: 'What is our refund policy?' → RAG retrieves refund policy document chunks → LLM generates accurate answer citing policy. Without RAG: LLM hallucinate karega generic policy. With RAG: accurate, grounded, citable. Enterprise AI ka backbone hai RAG.
how_to_answer: RAG: combine retrieval with generation for grounded responses
Pipeline: query → retrieve relevant documents → augment prompt → generate
Retrieval: embed documents, vector search for relevant chunks
Generation: LLM generates answer conditioned on retrieved context
Benefits: reduces hallucination, provides sources, up-to-date info
Components: vector DB (Pinecone/Weaviate) + embedding model + LLM
Challenges: retrieval quality, chunk size, context window limits

question: What are vector databases and why are they important for NLP?
hinglish_explanation: Vector databases embeddings store aur efficiently search karte hain. Millions of vectors mein nearest neighbors milliseconds mein dhundh lete hain. ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) algorithms use hote hain. RAG, semantic search, recommendation systems ka backbone hain. Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Qdrant popular hain.
real_life_example: E-commerce: 10 lakh products ke embeddings store. User search 'comfortable running shoes for flat feet' → vector search → semantically similar products instant results. Without vector DB: linear search = minutes. With: milliseconds. Flipkart/Amazon search internally similar systems use karte hain.
how_to_answer: Store and efficiently search high-dimensional vectors
Use cases: semantic search, RAG, recommendations, deduplication
ANN algorithms: HNSW, IVF, PQ for fast approximate search
Popular: Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Qdrant, ChromaDB
Features: metadata filtering, hybrid search, real-time updates
Scale: billions of vectors with sub-millisecond search
Critical for: RAG systems, semantic search, LLM applications

question: What is semantic search and how does it differ from keyword search?
hinglish_explanation: Keyword search: exact word match (BM25). Semantic search: meaning match (embeddings). 'Budget phone' semantic search mein 'affordable smartphone' bhi return karega even though words different hain. Dense retrieval models (DPR, SBERT) use hote hain. Modern: hybrid (keyword + semantic) best results deta hai.
real_life_example: Legal search: 'cases about tenant eviction' - keyword search misses 'landlord removing renter from property'. Semantic search meaning samajhke related cases dhundh leta hai. Casetext, Harvey AI legal semantic search use karte hain. Indian courts ke judgments search mein transformative.
how_to_answer: Semantic search: find results by meaning, not just keyword match
Keyword (BM25): exact/fuzzy term matching - fast, precise
Semantic (dense): embedding similarity - understands synonyms, paraphrases
Embedding models: SBERT, E5, BGE for document encoding
Index: vector database for ANN search on embeddings
Hybrid: combine BM25 + semantic scores for best results
Re-ranking: cross-encoder re-ranks top candidates for precision

question: What is the difference between bi-encoders and cross-encoders?
hinglish_explanation: Bi-encoder: query aur document independently encode, cosine similarity compare. Fast (pre-compute document embeddings). Cross-encoder: query+document together input, relevance score output. Slow but more accurate (sees token-level interactions). Best approach: bi-encoder retrieve top-100, cross-encoder re-rank top-10.
real_life_example: Search pipeline: 1M documents mein se relevant dhundhna. Step 1: Bi-encoder se top-100 retrieve (milliseconds, pre-computed embeddings). Step 2: Cross-encoder se top-100 re-rank (seconds, pair-wise comparison). Final top-10 = highly relevant. Two-stage retrieval pipeline industry standard hai.
how_to_answer: Bi-encoder: encode query and document independently, compare
Cross-encoder: encode query-document pair together, joint representation
Bi-encoder: fast (pre-compute), lower accuracy, scalable
Cross-encoder: slow (pairwise), higher accuracy, not scalable
Bi-encoder: SBERT, DPR → fast retrieval from millions
Cross-encoder: BERT pair classification → accurate re-ranking
Best practice: bi-encoder retrieve → cross-encoder re-rank

question: What is knowledge distillation for NLP models?
hinglish_explanation: Bada model (teacher) ka knowledge chhote model (student) mein transfer karna. Student teacher ke soft predictions (probability distributions) se seekhta hai - more information than hard labels. DistilBERT: BERT→6 layers, 97% quality. TinyBERT: task-specific distillation. Production deployment ke liye essential.
real_life_example: GPT-4 responses use karke chhota model train karo (distill) - Alpaca, Vicuna aise hi bane. Teacher GPT-4 (expensive, slow), Student: 7B model (cheap, fast) jo 80% quality retain kare. Cost: GPT-4 = $0.03/query, Distilled model = $0.001/query. 30x cheaper!
how_to_answer: Transfer knowledge from large teacher to small student model
Student learns from teacher's soft probability outputs
Soft labels contain more information than hard labels (dark knowledge)
Temperature parameter controls softness of distribution
Loss: α×distillation_loss + (1-α)×task_loss
Examples: DistilBERT, TinyBERT, MiniLM
Benefits: smaller, faster models retaining most of teacher quality

question: What is Sentence Transformers library and what models does it provide?
hinglish_explanation: Sentence Transformers: SBERT models ka library. Pre-trained models jo sentences ko embeddings mein convert karte hain. all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (fast, good quality), all-mpnet-base-v2 (best quality), multilingual models available. Semantic search, clustering, similarity sab 5 lines mein. sentence-transformers pip install karo.
real_life_example: FAQ matching system 5 lines mein: from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer; model = SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2'); embeddings = model.encode(faqs); query_emb = model.encode(question); results = cosine_similarity(query_emb, embeddings). Done!
how_to_answer: sentence-transformers: Python library for sentence/text embeddings
Pre-trained models optimized for semantic similarity
Popular models: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (fast), all-mpnet-base-v2 (quality)
Training: contrastive learning on NLI + semantic similarity data
Output: fixed-size dense vectors for sentences
Use cases: semantic search, clustering, paraphrase detection
Simple API: model.encode(sentences) → embeddings array

question: What is RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)?
hinglish_explanation: LLMs ko human preferences se align karna. Steps: (1) SFT - supervised fine-tuning on demonstrations. (2) Train reward model on human preference comparisons. (3) PPO optimize policy against reward model. ChatGPT isi technique se helpful/harmless bana. Without RLHF: model raw text complete karta, RLHF ke baad: helpful assistant banta hai.
real_life_example: GPT-3 (without RLHF): 'How to hack WiFi?' → detailed instructions de deta. ChatGPT (with RLHF): politely refuse karta hai. RLHF ne model ko harmful content refuse karna seekhaya. InstructGPT paper showed RLHF makes smaller model preferred over 100x larger model.
how_to_answer: RLHF: align LLMs with human preferences using RL
Step 1: SFT on demonstration data (supervised)
Step 2: Train reward model on human preference comparisons
Step 3: Optimize LLM policy using PPO against reward model
Makes models: helpful, harmless, honest
Alternative: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) - simpler, no RL
Critical for: safety, instruction following, conversational quality

question: What is the difference between open-source and closed-source LLMs?
hinglish_explanation: Closed: GPT-4, Claude - API access only, weights nahi milte, company controls everything. Open: LLaMA, Mistral, Falcon - weights download karo, locally run karo, modify karo. Open = privacy, customization, no API cost. Closed = best quality, no infra management. Trade-offs clear hain.
real_life_example: Banking app: customer data GPT-4 API pe bhej nahi sakte (privacy). Solution: LLaMA-7B locally deploy karo, LoRA fine-tune banking data pe, data premises pe rehta hai. Compliance satisfied, quality acceptable. Indian startups: Sarvam AI, Krutrim open models pe build kar rahe hain.
how_to_answer: Closed-source: API-only access (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini)
Open-source: weights available, local deployment possible
Open: LLaMA, Mistral, Falcon, Gemma, Qwen
Closed advantages: best quality, no infra management, easy start
Open advantages: privacy, customization, no per-token cost, control
Hybrid: use open for sensitive data, closed for complex reasoning
Trend: open models rapidly closing quality gap with closed

question: What is DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) and how does it compare to RLHF?
hinglish_explanation: DPO RLHF ka simplified version hai. RLHF: reward model train → PPO RL loop (complex, unstable). DPO: directly preference pairs se model optimize karo without separate reward model. Same result, simpler training. Loss function implicitly reward model embed karta hai. Zephyr, Intel Neural Chat DPO use karte hain.
real_life_example: LLaMA fine-tune karna hai alignment ke liye. RLHF: 3 stages, PPO unstable, hyperparameters bahut. DPO: preference pairs do (chosen vs rejected), one training loop, stable. Result similar quality. Most open-source aligned models ab DPO use karte hain simplicity ke liye.
how_to_answer: DPO: align LLMs with preferences without explicit reward model
RLHF: SFT → reward model → PPO (complex, unstable)
DPO: directly optimize on preference pairs (simpler, stable)
Input: pairs of (preferred response, rejected response)
Loss: implicitly parameterizes reward through policy
Advantages: simpler implementation, no RL instability, fewer hyperparams
Used by: Zephyr, Intel Neural Chat, many open-source alignments

question: What are embedding models for retrieval and what makes a good one?
hinglish_explanation: Retrieval embeddings: text ko vectors mein convert jaise ki similar text ke vectors close hon. Training: contrastive learning (positive pairs close, negative pairs far). Good model: high recall on retrieval benchmarks (MTEB). E5, BGE, GTE modern SOTA models hain. Different from general embeddings - retrieval-optimized.
real_life_example: RAG system ke liye embedding model choose: MTEB leaderboard dekho. BGE-large-en: best English retrieval. multilingual-e5-large: multilingual. Cohere embed-v3: commercial option. Query-document asymmetric embedding (query short, doc long) specialized models better handle karte hain.
how_to_answer: Embedding models optimized for retrieval/search tasks
Training: contrastive learning with in-batch negatives, hard negatives
Quality metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, Recall@k on MTEB/BEIR benchmarks
SOTA models: E5, BGE, GTE, Nomic-embed, Cohere embed
Characteristics of good retrieval embeddings: dimension, asymmetric handling
Instruction-tuned: prefix like 'query:' and 'passage:' for better performance
Open: sentence-transformers; Commercial: OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage

question: What is contrastive learning for text embeddings?
hinglish_explanation: Similar pairs (positive) ke embeddings close lao, dissimilar pairs (negative) ke embeddings door karo. SimCSE: same sentence twice pass (different dropout) = positive pair. Hard negatives: similar but irrelevant documents = best negatives. InfoNCE loss most common. SBERT, DPR, E5 sab contrastive learning use karte hain.
real_life_example: E-commerce search model training: query 'blue running shoes' + clicked product (positive), random product (negative). Hard negative: 'blue casual shoes' (similar but not what user wanted). Model seekhega exact intent match karna. Better negatives = better model.
how_to_answer: Contrastive learning: pull positives close, push negatives apart
InfoNCE/NT-Xent loss: softmax over similarity scores in batch
Positive pairs: paraphrases, query-document, augmented pairs
